In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Bench At Aurangabad Anticipatory Bail Application No. 1525 Of 2025 Sameer Jakiyyoddin Sayyad Versus The Superintendent Of Police And Another ... Advocate for Applicant : Mr. Rahul Pandhari Cheble App for Respondent/State : Mr. K.N. Lokhande ... Coram : Mehroz K. Pathan, J. Date : 6th November 2025 Per Court : 1. The Applicant has approached this Court, see anticipatory bail in connection with Crime No.274/2025 registered with Gandhi Chowk Police Station, District Latur for the offences punishable under Sections 123, 223, 274, 275 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and Section 59 of the Foods Safety and Standards Act, 2006. 2. texts.facts: The Applicant has approached this Court, see anticipatory bail in connection with Crime No.274/2025 registered with Gandhi Chowk Police Station, District Latur for the offences punishable under Sections 123, 223, 274, 275 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and Section 59 of the Foods Safety and Standards Act, 2006. 2. As per the First Information Report, the police authorities conducted a raid on the shop licensed in the name of the father of the present Applicant. The contraband, i.e., scented tobacco and pan masala worth Rs.5,860/-, was seized from the shop and has been sent to the Chemical Analyzer for obtaining its report. 3. The submission of the Counsel for the Applicant submits that 2 929.ABA-1525-2025.doc the shop is being run by Jakiyoddin Sayyad in whose name the license is issued under the Shop Act and the Applicant is doing a private business and has no share or interest in the running of the shop.
texts.arguments: He therefore submits that merely because the Applicant is the son of the licensee, he is being repeatedly dragged into various offences under the Shop Act. He further submits that as the Sameer Jakiyyoddin Sayyad vs The Superintendent Of Police And ... on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170975708/ 1 contraband is already seized nothing remains to be recovered at the instance of the Applicant and hence the custodial interrogation may not be necessary. 4. As against this, the learned APP submits that the offences are serious in nature as Section 328 IPC is attracted in the present case, there are criminal antecedents against the present Applicant, wherein the Applicant was prosecuted for identical offences under Sections 328 and relevant Sections of IPC as well as the Food Safety and Standards Act. 5. The Counsel for the Applicant submits that the Applicant though was earlier also implicated in identical offences, this Court has granted him bail.
